The evidence collectively shows the alliance evolved through multiple stages rather than a single date. The United States and the United Kingdom have been durable partners and allies since reestablishing diplomatic relations in 1815 after the War of 1812 [d1, d3]. The alliance strengthened significantly through cooperation in World War I [d7, d8] and was cemented during World War II with the Lend-Lease program in 1940 and the close Churchill-Roosevelt "special relationship" [d5, d6, d8]. Some sources also point to growing alignment around the turn of the 20th century, such as the 1890s [d4, d9]. Thus, the relationship evolved over more than a century into the firm alliance described today [d3, d8].
